description: Historical index membership, survivorship-free: who was in an index on `as_of_date` (companies that existed and belonged on that exact date, including ones delisted since; no hindsight). Use it INSTEAD OF `search_companies` for any past date ("Was X in the S&P 500 on Y?"); `search_companies` knows only current membership. To check one company, pass `ticker` (better, a CIK) + `index` + the date: present = member. Coverage: S&P 500 members on a date, including former members, from 1996 (reconstructed, incomplete before about 2007); Russell 1000/2000/3000 from 2000-09-30 at medium confidence. Each result's `note` states the depth and gaps of the index asked about: read it before a backtest. Branch on `_meta.pit_safe` (false = approximate; always false for Russell) and each row's `confidence`. A response is one PAGE: `complete` and `survivorship_free` are true only when `returned_rows` equals `universe_size`; page with `offset` = `truncation.next_offset`, or read the whole table with `get_compute_ready_stream`. Carry each row's `cik`; `enriched: false` is a member whose identity is unknown, still a member. `sector` is SIC-derived, not GICS. Plan: every plan; without sign-in it returns the subset that coverage includes.

as_of_date.description: Historical date (YYYY-MM-DD) for survivorship-free construction. Index queries use index_membership join/leave dates (entrants after the date excluded, later-removed members kept); sector queries use security valid_from/valid_to. Omit for the current universe.

include_share_classes.description: false (default) collapses to one row per CIK (index-provider convention — BRK counts once, not BRK-A + BRK-B). true returns every share-class row (GOOG and GOOGL separately) — for security-level analysis only.

index.description: Index filter. 'sp500' (~500 large caps; reconstructed history from 1996, incomplete before ~2007, check pit_safe), 'russell1000' (~1000 large/mid), 'russell2000' (~2000 small caps), 'russell3000' (~3000 broad market) — the three Russell indices carry fund-derived history back to 2000-09-30 at medium confidence, with observation spacing that widens before 2007. Omit for no index filter (sector-only or full universe queries).

is_active.description: Filter to active (currently trading) companies only. Omit to include all. WARNING: setting this to true on a HISTORICAL query reintroduces survivorship bias — companies that were active on as_of_date but later went bankrupt or got acquired will be filtered out.  Leave unset for true PIT backtests.

limit.description: Rows per page (1–3500; at most 250 are inlined per call). Defaults to 100. `universe_size` always states the full matched count; when more rows remain after this page the response carries a `truncation` envelope — call again with `offset` = its `next_offset`. Universe is deduped to one row per CIK (SP500 ~505, Russell 3000 ~3050).

offset.description: Zero-based row offset where this page starts. Pass the previous response's `truncation.next_offset` to fetch the next page. Defaults to 0.

sector.description: Sector filter (case-insensitive substring) over the SIC-derived, GICS-aligned label (not licensed GICS — see tool description). E.g. 'Technology', 'Energy'.

ticker.description: Check ONE company: a ticker or a CIK (SEC identifier), e.g. 'AAPL' or '0000320193'. Returns that company's row if it was a member on as_of_date, none if it was not. A ticker matches the symbol listed ON that date, and a since-delisted member can carry no ticker at all (enriched=false), so prefer the CIK for historical checks. Omit to list the universe.

name: get_pit_universe

_meta.description: Response metadata (provenance, point-in-time flag, freshness, request id and warnings). Every field is documented once in the agent contract (agent_contract.meta in the server's manifest.json).

truncation.description: Present only when the inline-row cap withheld rows. Page with `next_offset` (keep the same `limit`) or pull the full set via get_compute_ready_stream.
